_comment: Plain-language explanations of common processes, per OS. advice: keep (part of the OS, ending it breaks things or logs you out), restarts (safe to end, the OS starts it again), quit (an app or helper you can quit; save your work first). Generated into each UI by scripts/gen-catalog.py.

macos.description: The macOS kernel. Its CPU use also covers throttling the CPU when the Mac runs hot.
Starts and supervises every other process and background service.
Draws every window on screen. High CPU usually means many windows, displays or animations.
Your login session. Ending it logs you out.
The Finder: desktop, file windows and file operations.
The Dock, Launchpad, Mission Control and full-screen spaces.
Shows system items in the menu bar.
Control Center and the menu bar's clock, Wi‑Fi and sound items.
Shows notifications and widgets.
Stage Manager and window tiling.
The Spotlight search window.
Spotlight indexing. Busy after updates or when many files change; it calms down once the index is current.
All sound in and out of the Mac. Ending it briefly cuts audio.
Bluetooth: keyboards, mice, headphones.
Wi‑Fi connections and scanning.
Keeps network and system configuration up to date.
Looks up domain names (DNS) and finds devices on the local network (Bonjour).
Passes notifications between processes.
Reads and writes app and system preferences.
Certificates, the keychain and code signatures.
Checks apps before they run (Gatekeeper, XProtect malware scanning).
Privacy permissions: camera, microphone, files, screen recording.
User accounts, groups and login checks.
Power management: sleep, battery and what keeps the Mac awake.
Collects the system log.
Decides how much CPU and memory each app may use, and suspends idle ones.
Watches temperatures and slows the Mac down when it gets too hot.
Tells apps which files changed (Spotlight, Time Machine, sync apps rely on it).
Time Machine backups. Busy while a backup runs.
iCloud Drive and other cloud folders syncing files.
Analyses photos for faces, objects and Memories. Runs mostly while the Mac is idle and plugged in.
Downloads macOS updates and system data files.
Background downloads for apps and the system.
AirDrop, Handoff and sharing between your devices.
Talks to your other Apple devices nearby (Continuity, Universal Clipboard).
Apple push notifications for apps.
iMessage, FaceTime and calls relayed from your iPhone.
Location Services.
Knows which app opens which file, and launches apps.
Reacts to system events (devices plugged in, network changes) for your session.
Loads kernel and system extensions (drivers).
Network health, VPN and proxy support.
The macOS firewall.
Keyboard, mouse and trackpad input.
Display brightness and Night Shift.
Accessibility features such as VoiceOver and zoom.
Manages installed fonts.
Quick Look previews and file thumbnails.
Writes crash and hang reports. Busy right after an app crashes or freezes.
Frees disk space by removing purgeable files when the disk gets full.
Siri, suggestions and on-device learning about how you use the Mac.
Your Apple Account and internet accounts.
Keeps the clock in sync.
Enforces the app sandbox.
Restarts the Mac if the system stops responding.
Screen Sharing (someone viewing or controlling this Mac).
A web page open in Safari or an app that shows web content. Ending it reloads that page.
Network or graphics work for web content in Safari and other apps.
Part of Chrome: one helper per tab, extension or GPU task. Ending a renderer closes that tab's page.
Part of Visual Studio Code: windows, extensions and language servers.
A virtual machine (used by Docker, Podman, UTM and others). Ending it shuts the VM down hard.
Docker Desktop and its Linux virtual machine.
Procyon itself, and its helper for full access.
